texts.li:
"I was aiming at the post."
"The post is over there."

{A_nameDef} ran when the window went, then came back on {A_possessive} own, which {B_nameDef} counts in {A_possessive} favor. {B_nameDef} has brought it to the council anyway, mostly to see what the council will say.

The chickens are out, the rain barrel is over, and the cook's bread has gone from the step. Every track leads to {A_nameDef}, who says it was an experiment. {B_nameDef} would like the council to decide what experiments are for.

[lowtech] {A_nameDef} tried to climb onto the storehouse roof to see the hills and brought half the thatch down with {A_objective}. {A_nameDef} is fine. The roof is not. {B_nameDef} wants the council's word on it.

li.label: {A_nameDef} mends it, with {B_nameDef}'s help
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} spent the afternoon with {B_nameDef}, putting right what {A_pronoun} broke. {B_nameDef} showed {A_objective} how, and made {A_objective} do every bit of it, twice where the first try came out crooked.

outcomes.li: [b:quirk:Proverbs] "You break it, you mend it, you learn it," {B_nameDef} said, and said it again every time {A_nameDef} complained. {A_nameDef} mended it. {A_nameDef} can now recite the saying in {B_nameDef}'s voice.
[b:trait:Abrasive] {B_nameDef} stood over {A_nameDef} the whole time with a running commentary on everything {A_pronoun} did wrong. It's mended. It's mended very well.

li.label: Say sorry to everyone at supper
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} stood up at supper and said sorry to the whole colony, in a very small voice. Someone clapped. {A_nameDef} went red to the ears, and won't do it again in a hurry.

outcomes.li: [quirk:WrongLaugh] {A_nameDef} got halfway through saying sorry at supper and started giggling, and couldn't stop, and set off half the table. It wasn't much of an apology. It was a very good supper.

li.label: Children break things. Let it go.
li.outcome: Children break things and grown-ups mend them, the council said, and that was the end of it. {B_nameDef} did the mending, muttering, while {A_nameDef} handed up the nails.
li.riskOutcome: The council let it go, and {A_nameDef} took that as permission. Two days later it was the rain barrel again. {B_nameDef} hasn't said "I told you so" yet, out loud.

li.label: A stern word from the council
li.outcome: The council gave {A_nameDef} a stern talking-to, all of them at once, which was a lot of stern for one small person. {A_nameDef} hasn't thrown a stone since. {A_nameDef} hasn't said much since, either.

texts.li: Every noise in the night has {A_nameDef} sitting up in bed, staring at the door. This morning {A_pronoun} wouldn't go out past it. {B_nameDef} has tried everything {B_pronoun} can think of, and has come to the council.

{A_nameDef} saw more of the attack than a child should, from a window nobody thought to cover. Now {A_pronoun} hides under the table at every loud noise. {B_nameDef} wants to know what the colony can do for {A_objective}.
[night] It's late, and {A_nameDef} is still awake, sitting up with a stick across {A_possessive} knees "in case they come back". {B_nameDef} has asked the council, quietly, what to do.

li.label: {B_nameDef} sits up with {A_nameDef} tonight
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} sat up with {A_nameDef} through the night, with a light burning and a long story about nothing much. {A_nameDef} fell asleep somewhere in the middle of it, holding {B_nameDef}'s sleeve.

outcomes.li: [b:quirk:Storyteller] {B_nameDef} sat up with {A_nameDef} and told the old story about the brave mouse, the long version, with all the voices. {A_nameDef} was asleep before the mouse reached the river.

[b:quirk:NightLight] {B_nameDef} brought {A_nameDef} the little lamp {B_pronoun} keeps by {B_possessive} own bed, and said it had kept the bad dreams away for years. {A_nameDef} slept with it clutched in both hands.

li.label: Stories round the fire for all the children
li.outcome: The colony lit a fire in the evening and the children sat close to it while the grown-ups told stories, none of them about raiders. {A_nameDef} laughed twice, once at a story that wasn't meant to be funny.

outcomes.li: [b:quirk:Storyteller] {B_nameDef} told the stories round the fire, one after another, until the children were asleep in a heap. {A_nameDef} was the last to go, and asked for one more.

li.label: Show {A_nameDef} the walls and the watch
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} walked {A_nameDef} round the walls and showed {A_objective} where the watch stands, and the gate, and how it bars. {A_nameDef} asked a hundred questions and seemed to feel better for every answer.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] {B_nameDef} walked {A_nameDef} round the palisade and let {A_objective} knock on every post to hear how solid it was. They're all solid. {A_nameDef} checked twice.

li.label: Children get over these things
li.outcome: The council said children are tougher than they look and {A_nameDef} would get over it. {A_nameDef} is still awake at night. {B_nameDef} has stopped asking.

texts.li: Since the death, {A_nameDef} has gone very quiet: eats, works at {A_possessive} lessons, goes to bed, and doesn't say a word about it. {B_nameDef} thinks that's the worrying part.
{A_nameDef} keeps asking when the dead one is coming back, and every time someone tells {A_objective}, {A_pronoun} cries like it's the first time. {B_nameDef} has run out of ways to say it.
{A_nameDef} has been setting out a cup at supper for someone who isn't coming. None of the grown-ups has had the heart to take it away. {B_nameDef} wants to know if someone should.

li.label: {B_nameDef} takes {A_nameDef} under {B_possessive} wing
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} has been with {A_nameDef} as much as the work allows: meals together, walks, a hand on the shoulder at the bad moments. At bedtime now, {A_nameDef} has started to talk about it, in pieces.

outcomes.li: [b:trait:Kind] {B_nameDef} simply stopped leaving {A_nameDef} alone, gently, all day. By evening {A_nameDef} was talking, and by bedtime, crying at last.

li.label: A goodbye at the grave, with {A_nameDef}
li.outcome: The colony walked out to the grave with {A_nameDef}, and {A_nameDef} said goodbye properly, with a flower and a stone and some words {A_pronoun} had practiced. It was hard. {A_nameDef} slept that night.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] They walked to the grave with {A_nameDef}, and {A_nameDef} put a little carved animal on it, so the dead one wouldn't be lonely. One by one the others left something too.

li.label: Keep {A_nameDef} busy with lessons
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} has a full day of lessons now, from breakfast until dark. {A_nameDef} is learning a great deal. {A_nameDef} still hasn't cried. {B_nameDef} isn't sure that's a good thing.

li.label: Time will do it
li.outcome: The council decided time would do what words couldn't. {A_nameDef} goes to bed early these days, and lies awake.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} can't read the labels on the crates, {B_nameDef} has noticed, because no one has ever taught {A_objective}. {B_nameDef} offers to give the children lessons every morning, if the council will spare the hours.
{A_nameDef} asked {B_nameDef} what the marks in a book mean, and {B_nameDef} realized the children here have been taught nothing but chores. {B_nameDef} has a plan, and wants the council's blessing.
[lowtech] {B_nameDef} wants to teach the children their letters, the counting of seasons and the names of the stars. "Or they'll grow up knowing only how to dig," {B_nameDef} told the council.
[colony:Hardworking] In a colony where everyone works from dawn, {B_nameDef} has asked for something unusual: two hours each morning for the children to learn, starting with {A_nameDef}.

li.label: Morning lessons, with {B_nameDef}
li.outcome: Every morning now, {B_nameDef} sits the children down for lessons, starting with {A_nameDef}. They grumble about it. They also correct the grown-ups' spelling.

outcomes.li: [b:quirk:KeepsRecords] {B_nameDef} keeps a ledger of every lesson and every child's progress, in columns. {A_nameDef} has started a ledger of {B_nameDef}'s sayings.
[b:quirk:Proverbs] {B_nameDef}'s lessons are half letters and half old sayings. The children can't spell yet, but they all know that a cold oven bakes no bread.

li.label: They learn by working beside us
li.outcome: The council decided the children learn best at the grown-ups' elbows, doing real work. {A_nameDef} spent the day following the builders about. {B_nameDef} thinks it's a mistake, and said so.

li.label: Let them run free a while yet
li.outcome: Lessons can wait, the council said; the children should have the run of the place while they're small. {A_nameDef} took that very seriously and spent the day up a tree.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} built a den together behind the woodpile, and now each of them says it's theirs. There has been shouting, kicking of the den, and a strongly worded complaint to the council from both sides.

{A_nameDef} found a beautiful stone by the river. {B_nameDef} says {B_pronoun} saw it first. The stone is now in the council's keeping until the matter is settled, and both children are waiting outside.

[winter] The two children have been cooped up indoors for days and are at each other's throats. Today it was over who gets the seat by the window. {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} have each brought a petition. Both are written in charcoal.

li.label: They share it, and that's that
li.outcome: The council said they'd share it, and set out the rules: whose turn, how long, no kicking. {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} sulked until lunch and were seen playing in it together by supper.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} took turns, as ordered, for exactly one day. Then the shouting started again, and the den is now a pile of sticks.

li.label: Help them build a second one
li.outcome: A grown-up gave up an afternoon and a stack of wood, and now there are two dens behind the woodpile. {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} visit each other's, formally, with knocks.

li.label: Let them sort it out themselves
li.outcome: Left to sort it out themselves, they did, eventually, after a great deal of noise. What they agreed is between the two of them.
li.riskOutcome: They sorted it out themselves, which meant {B_nameDef} pushed {A_nameDef} into a puddle, and they haven't spoken since.

ColonyCouncil.DilemmaDef.label: a youngster who wants to see the world

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has never been further than the fields, and wants to go out with the next caravan, or the next anything. {B_nameDef} says {A_nameDef} is far too young. {A_nameDef} says {B_nameDef} was younger when {B_pronoun} left home.

Every trader and traveler who comes by gets the same questions from {A_nameDef}, where they've been and how far and what it was like. Now {A_nameDef} wants to go and see the world {A_objective}self. {B_nameDef} has asked the council to say no. {A_nameDef} has asked the council to say yes.
[colony:Restless] The young ones are always looking at the road. {A_nameDef} has packed a bag, and asked the council's leave before using it. {B_nameDef} is beside {A_objective}, arms folded.

li.label: {A_nameDef} goes with the next journey out
li.outcome: Yes, the council said: when someone next sets out from the colony, {A_nameDef} may go along. {A_nameDef}'s bag was packed by nightfall. {B_nameDef} has been quiet.

outcomes.li: [b:quirk:Worrier] The council said yes. {B_nameDef} has made {A_nameDef} a list of everything that could go wrong on the road, and a second list of what to do about each one. {A_nameDef} has packed both.

li.label: Not this year
li.outcome: Not this year, the council said. {A_nameDef} took the bag back to {A_possessive} room and has been short with everyone since. {B_nameDef} looks relieved, and guilty about it.

li.label: A long walk past the fields with {B_nameDef}, first
li.outcome: A day's walk out past the fields, with {B_nameDef}, to start with. They came back at dusk, muddy, still talking. {A_nameDef} wants to go further. {B_nameDef} has stopped saying never.

li.label: a long walk past the fields

ColonyCouncil.DilemmaDef.label: one last look at the hills

texts.li: "While my legs still go." {A_nameDef} wants a day off to walk out to the hills at the edge of the colony's land, the way {A_pronoun} used to when {A_pronoun} first came. {B_nameDef} has offered to go along.

{A_nameDef} wants to see the place where the colony first camped, out past the fields, once more. It's a long walk for old legs. {B_nameDef} says {B_pronoun}'ll carry {A_nameDef} if it comes to that. {A_nameDef} says it won't.

[spring] The hills are green again, and {A_nameDef} has asked to walk out and see them, the way {A_pronoun} has every spring for years. This year {A_pronoun} needs a stick. {B_nameDef} would like to go too.

li.label: {B_nameDef} goes with {A_nameDef} for the day
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} walked out to the hills and sat a long while at the top, and {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} about the first days, when there was nothing here but grass. They came back slowly, after dark, and {A_nameDef} slept like a child.

outcomes.li: [quirk:Proverbs] At the top of the hill {A_nameDef} looked back at the colony and said "a house is built of stones, a home of years." {B_nameDef} has been repeating it to everyone since.
[b:quirk:KeepsRecords] {B_nameDef} wrote down everything {A_nameDef} said on the hill, every name and every date. It's the first true history of the colony, and it fits in one notebook.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} go alone, as {A_pronoun} asks
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} went alone, slowly, with a stick and a heel of bread, and came back at dusk tired and quiet and pleased with {A_objective}self.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} went alone and got halfway before {A_possessive} knees gave up the argument. {A_nameDef} sat on a rock until someone came looking, and was walked home between two people, saying very little.

li.label: It's too far; stay where it's safe
li.outcome: Too far, and too risky. {A_nameDef} heard the council out, went to sit by the wall, and looked at the hills all afternoon.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has {ILLNESS} and won't let {B_nameDef} look at it. "I've had worse than this and lived," {A_nameDef} says, and goes on working, slower every day. {B_nameDef} has asked the council to make {A_objective} see sense.
{B_nameDef} has been trying for days to get a look at {A_nameDef}'s {ILLNESS}. {A_nameDef} keeps finding urgent work at the other end of the colony. {B_nameDef} wants the council's backing.

[lowtech] {A_nameDef} is treating {A_possessive} {ILLNESS} with an old family cure that smells terrible, and won't hear of anything else. {B_nameDef} has come to the council with a basket of proper herbs and a very tired face.

li.label: Insist: {B_nameDef} sees to {A_nameDef} today
li.outcome: The council insisted. {A_nameDef} sat for {B_nameDef}'s examination with the face of someone being robbed, and was given rest and a remedy. {A_nameDef} feels better, and is more put out than ever.

outcomes.li: [quirk:Proverbs] {A_nameDef} submitted to {B_nameDef}'s examination with a running commentary of sayings about doctors, none of them kind. {B_nameDef} has heard them all before.

li.label: Respect {A_nameDef}'s wishes
li.outcome: The council said {A_nameDef} is grown and knows {A_possessive} own body. {A_nameDef} thanked them stiffly. {B_nameDef} has taken to leaving remedies where {A_nameDef} will find them.

li.label: Strike a bargain: a check-up for a favor
li.outcome: The council brokered a deal: {A_nameDef} lets {B_nameDef} look, and in return {B_nameDef} takes {A_nameDef}'s turn at the worst chore for a week. {A_nameDef} held out for two weeks, settled for one, and sat for the examination looking pleased with {A_objective}self.

texts.li: Give {A_nameDef} one evening, with everyone together, and {A_pronoun} will tell the colony's story from the very beginning, the way {A_pronoun} remembers it, before it's forgotten. {B_nameDef} thinks it should be written down too.

"Half the people at that table don't know how this place started," {A_nameDef} told the council, "and I'm one of the last who does." {A_nameDef} wants to tell it, once, to everyone. {B_nameDef} has offered to keep a record.

[winter] The nights are long, and {A_nameDef} has asked to spend one of them telling the colony's history to everyone, the whole of it, with the cold kept out by the fire. {B_nameDef} would like to take it down as {A_pronoun} speaks.

li.label: Everyone gathers to hear it
li.outcome: The whole colony gathered in the evening, and {A_nameDef} told the story of the colony from the first day, the hard winters and the good harvests and the people who aren't here anymore. It went on long past the usual bedtime, and some of the young ones cried at parts they'd never heard.

outcomes.li: [quirk:Proverbs] {A_nameDef} told the colony's story with a saying for every hard year. By the end the whole room was saying them along with {A_objective}.
[quirk:WrongLaugh] {A_nameDef} told the colony's story and laughed at all the wrong places, the sad ones especially. By the end the room was laughing with {A_objective}, and some of them crying too.
[lowtech] {A_nameDef} told it the old way, by the fire, with a stick to point at the shadows. The children will be telling it to their children.

li.label: {B_nameDef} writes it all down
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} sat with {A_nameDef} for three evenings and wrote down everything: names, dates, the winter that nearly finished them. It's the colony's first history. {A_nameDef} has read it twice and corrected it four times.

outcomes.li: [b:quirk:KeepsRecords] {B_nameDef} had been waiting for this. {B_nameDef} wrote down everything {A_nameDef} said, then cross-checked it against {B_possessive} own notes and found six mistakes, all of them {A_nameDef}'s. They're still arguing about four.

li.label: Another time
li.outcome: The council said there'd be time for stories when the work was done. {A_nameDef} nodded, and didn't ask again.

ColonyCouncil.DilemmaDef.label: the old one and the little one

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has taken a shine to {B_nameDef}, and wants to teach {B_objective} what {A_pronoun} knows, a little every day. Some of the grown-ups think the child should be with other children, or at lessons, not following an old one about.

{B_nameDef} has been sitting with {A_nameDef} every afternoon, watching {A_objective} work and asking questions. {A_nameDef} asks the council's leave to make it proper: a pupil, and a teacher with time to spare.

[quirk:Storyteller] {B_nameDef} turns up at {A_nameDef}'s chair every evening for a story, and every evening {A_nameDef} slips a lesson into it. {A_nameDef} wants the council's leave to make the lessons proper ones.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} teach {B_nameDef}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} teaches {B_nameDef} an hour or two each afternoon now, slowly, and {B_nameDef} has the patience for it that the grown-ups never did. Both of them look forward to it more than they'll say.

outcomes.li: [quirk:Proverbs] {A_nameDef} teaches {B_nameDef} a skill and a proverb every afternoon. {B_nameDef} is learning both, and using the proverbs on the grown-ups, who don't like it.

li.label: Ask {B_nameDef}'s family first
li.outcome: The council sent {A_nameDef} to ask {B_nameDef}'s family first. They said yes, after some thought. {A_nameDef} was hurt to have been made to ask, and pleased to have been allowed.

li.label: Children belong with children
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} belongs with the other children, at lessons and games, the council said. {A_nameDef} said nothing. {B_nameDef} still turns up at {A_nameDef}'s chair in the evenings, when the grown-ups aren't looking.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} can't get warm: sleeps in {A_possessive} coat, eats beside the stove and still shivers at night. {B_nameDef} has noticed, and come to the council about it before {A_nameDef} would.
The cold has got into {A_nameDef}'s joints, and some mornings {A_pronoun} can't close {A_possessive} hands until noon. {B_nameDef} wants to know what the colony can spare to keep {A_objective} warm.
[lowtech] {A_nameDef} has taken to sleeping by the hearth, rolled in every blanket {A_pronoun} owns, and is still cold. {B_nameDef} wants more wood for {A_objective}, or a warmer bed, or both.

li.label: Burn extra wood for {A_nameDef}
li.outcome: Extra firewood was set aside to keep {A_nameDef}'s room warm through the cold months. {A_nameDef} grumbled about the waste, and then slept like a stone.

li.label: {B_nameDef} gives up the warmer room
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} offered {A_nameDef} the room nearest the stove and took a colder one {B_objective}self. {A_nameDef} refused twice, then accepted, then said thank you three times.

outcomes.li: [b:quirk:Volunteers] {B_nameDef} had already moved {B_possessive} things out of the warm room before the council finished talking. {A_nameDef} found the bed made and a hot stone in it.

li.label: {B_nameDef} sits with {A_nameDef} by the fire in the evenings
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} sits with {A_nameDef} by the fire in the evenings now, keeping it fed and keeping {A_objective} company. Some evenings they talk. Most evenings {A_nameDef} dozes and {B_nameDef} minds the fire.

li.label: Everyone's cold. {A_nameDef} will manage.
li.outcome: The council said the whole colony is cold and there's no wood to spare for one person. {A_nameDef} said {A_pronoun} understood. {A_nameDef} is still cold.

ColonyCouncil.DilemmaDef.label: the old way and the new

texts.li: For thirty years {A_nameDef} has done the job one way. {B_nameDef} has a new way, quicker, and has been doing it behind {A_nameDef}'s back. Now {A_nameDef} has found out, and both of them are in front of the council, not looking at each other.

{B_nameDef} says {A_nameDef}'s way of storing the grain is why half of it spoiled. {A_nameDef} says {B_nameDef} wasn't born when {A_pronoun} started storing grain. Both want the council to say who's right.
[quirk:Proverbs] {A_nameDef} answered {B_nameDef}'s new idea with "if it isn't broken, don't fix it," for the ninth time this week. {B_nameDef} has had enough, and brought it to the council.

li.label: The old way: {A_nameDef} has done it longer
li.outcome: The council backed {A_nameDef}. It's done the old way, as it always has been. {A_nameDef} was gracious about winning, mostly. {B_nameDef} is doing it the old way, loudly.

li.label: The new way: let {B_nameDef} try it
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} gets a season to do it {B_possessive} way. {B_nameDef} is delighted. {A_nameDef} is keeping a close eye on it, and a list.

outcomes.li: [quirk:KeepsRecords] {A_nameDef} has started a page in {A_possessive} notebook headed "the new way: what went wrong". It's blank so far, which annoys {A_objective}.

li.label: Work it out together
li.outcome: The council sent them both off to work it out together. They argued for a day, worked side by side for another, and came back with a way that was half of each. Neither of them will admit the other was right about anything.
li.riskOutcome: The council sent them to work it out together, and they spent the whole day arguing and the job didn't get done. They're barely speaking.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} hasn't slept properly in a week for listening to the night, and has asked the council for a watch on the walls every night, with {A_objective}self on it if need be. {B_nameDef} says the colony can't spare the sleep.

{A_nameDef}'s list of what could come over the walls at night, in order of likelihood:

Raiders.
Something hungry, on four legs.
Raiders who heard the first ones did well.
Fire.

It runs to two pages. {A_nameDef} wants a night watch. {B_nameDef}, who would be standing it, doesn't.
[afterraid] Since the last attack, {A_nameDef} checks the doors four times before bed and still lies awake. {A_nameDef} asks for a night watch, just for a while. {B_nameDef} would take a turn.

li.label: Set a night watch for a while
li.outcome: The council set a night watch for the next few weeks, with {B_nameDef} taking the first turns. {A_nameDef} slept through the night for the first time in a week. {B_nameDef} didn't.

li.label: the first night watch on the walls
{B_nameDef} talks it through with {A_nameDef}
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} sat down with {A_nameDef} and went through every fear, one at a time, and what the colony would do about each. By the end {A_nameDef} was laughing at some of them. {A_nameDef} still checks the doors, but only twice.

li.label: The walls are fine. Get some sleep.
li.outcome: The council told {A_nameDef} the walls are fine and everyone needs their sleep. {A_nameDef} said thank you, and lay awake listening anyway.

texts.li: From {A_nameDef}'s notebook, a page picked at random: "Rain. Two crates moved to the back shelf. {B_nameDef} late to breakfast, third time this week."\n\n{A_nameDef} wants it made official: the colony's record, kept by {A_objective} and read out at the year's end. {B_nameDef} says some things are better not written down.

{B_nameDef} found {B_possessive} own name in {A_nameDef}'s notebook, with a date and an unflattering remark. {B_nameDef} wants the notebook burned. {A_nameDef} wants it made the colony's official history.

li.label: Make {A_nameDef} keeper of the colony's record
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is the colony's record keeper now, by the council's word. The notebook has a shelf of its own. {B_nameDef} has been very careful what {B_pronoun} says at supper.

li.label: Keep it, but keep it private
li.outcome: The council said {A_nameDef} can write what {A_pronoun} likes, as long as no one else has to read it. {A_nameDef} has started a second notebook about the council.

li.label: Read out the good parts at supper
li.outcome: The council asked {A_nameDef} to read out the kindest pages at supper. There were a good many of them. {B_nameDef} came out of it rather well, and asked for a copy.

li.label: a reading from the colony's record
